rav.text: Jace Beleren is drawn into Ravnica's guild struggle when Ral Zarek discovers the Implicit Maze on Niv-Mizzet's instruction, using Jace's notes.
When the runners gather at the Forum of Azor, Jace discovers the Bailiff and learns of the Supreme Verdict, while Lazav also speaks to the Bailiff.

The Bailiff pronounces the Supreme Verdict, and to prevent catastrophe Jace links the minds of all ten runners at the cost of nearly unraveling his own, after which he is declared the new Living Guildpact.

Afterward Jace honors Emmara Tandris's request to erase her knowledge of planeswalkers, and the Chamber of the Guildpact is raised in Gateway Plaza on the ashes of his former sanctum, a site he tells Lavinia seemed fitting.

fut.text: Jace Beleren is born on Vryn and later becomes an employee of the Infinite Consortium, only to defect and join Liliana in dethroning Tezzeret.
He erases his memory and loses six months of his life, and he later merges the maze-runners' minds to stop violence at the Forum of Azor, becoming Living Guildpact.

m10.text: Jace Beleren appears as a mind-mage who muses on the nature of thought, saying "All consciousness is one, separated only by a thin veil of the physical."
He is just as blunt about his craft, asking "Why fight the body when you can dominate the mind that rules it?"

Writers of the time note that he can create illusions without having met the creature they depict, though even proficient mind-mages like him have a limited range, so learning a summoning means planeswalking to the plane itself.

zen.text: Jace Beleren and Chandra defeat Sarkhan at the Eye of Ugin, and later Jace pitches a hedron trap to the Zendikari even as Kiora insists on attacking Ulamog with the bident and Nissa objects to trapping the titan.

When the ring fails to light because of a misaligned hedron, Nissa shares Jace's mind and illusion so they can find the tilted stone, and Gideon holds out against Ulamog until the titan is pulled into the glowing prison.

Ob Nixilis senses a telepath in his head and strikes Jace down, breaking his cheekbone, and the planeswalkers hang helpless in midair until Chandra arrives, Jace tells her by telepathy to burn the Eldrazi drones, and the four together defeat the demon.

Jace suggests leaving Zendikar to its fate, but Nissa refuses and Gideon argues that four can stand together, so Jace swears the oath to keep watch, then announces that since the titans cannot be trapped they will be killed, and joins Nissa in a plan that binds them with Zendikar's leylines at its last stand.

wwk.text: Jace Beleren appears on this set's cards as a planeswalker who comments on memory and on nature's wrath against magic users on Zendikar.

m11.text: Jace Beleren is overpowered on Ravnica by Garruk, who is seeking a cure and comes to his senses afterward, then learns Liliana's last location.
On the set's cards Jace speaks of the mind as a weapon and of Chandra's mind.

m12.text: After turning against and defeating Tezzeret, Jace Beleren became the de facto leader of the Consortium's Ravnica cell and put its resources to work.
When Chandra stole a scroll from the Sanctum of Stars on Kephalai, Jace was hired to recover it, which led both planeswalkers to the Eye of Ugin on Zendikar.
Jace is no gentler with Garruk Wildspeaker, belittling him because he has "only recently begun to walk upright" and explaining a simple thing slowly.
The set also brings Jace back in a new version, alongside Chandra and Garruk, while Gideon and Sorin replace Ajani and Liliana.

rtr.text: Jace Beleren marches into the depths of Ravnica in search of powerful magic and the code built into the city, deciding not to include his friends in so dangerous a quest.

He tries to retreat from the guild war but is pulled back when Emmara Tandris is kidnapped by the Cult of Rakdos, and he erases six months of his memory before Ral Zarek forces him to reveal to Emmara that he is a planeswalker.
At the Forum of Azor Jace links the maze-runners' minds, and the Bailiff declares him the new Guildpact.
At her request he erases Emmara's memories of other worlds and planeswalkers, and he also neutralizes Vraska, who had tried to control the Living Guildpact.

dgm.text: Jace Beleren's notes set the maze in motion, as Ral Zarek discovers it on Niv-Mizzet's instruction.
Lavinia is chosen to run the maze for the Azorius and arrests Jace at the Azorius Guildgate, and Isperia sentences him to community service.
When Lazav causes mayhem as Teysa completes the maze, Jace links the maze-runners' minds, triggering the Supreme Verdict and becoming the first Living Guildpact.
Lavinia then becomes his aide and deputy.

bng.text: Jace Beleren arrives late at the Chamber of the Guildpact to find Boros minotaurs complaining that the Orzhov violated a boundary contract, and he rules that they must file a proper complaint with Lavinia.

Lavinia then shows him petrified victims in Rozlad Square arranged to spell his name, and Jace, recognizing that their names match planes and that a planeswalker is targeting him, insists on going there alone.

In the square Vraska reveals herself as a gorgon and planeswalker who wants Jace to prove he will be an ally of Ravnica, but the Jace she faces is only an illusion, and the real Jace deduces that she wants to control him as Guildpact.

When she strangles him he sends image after image of himself at her, and the petrified statues speak in his voice and trick her into explaining her plan to take over Ravnica, all of it broadcast to the guild leaders at Sunhome, so she planeswalks away and Jace returns to the Chamber uneasy about Garruk.

ori.text: Jace Beleren learns that his spark ignited a year earlier and that the sphinx Alhammarret lied to him, so in rage he destroys Alhammarret's mind in a telepathic duel, accidentally planeswalks to Ravnica, and erases his own memories of what he had done.

Later, ordered to manipulate Talqez, Jace snaps and flees the Infinite Consortium with Kallist, but Liliana secretly informs the Consortium of their location and, when agents attack, Jace's mind-merge with Kallist fails and swaps their identities.

Liliana has Jace's friends assassinated, so Jace breaks into the Ravnica headquarters and wipes out the Consortium's Ravnican heads, and once she confesses that she needs the Consortium to escape her demon pact, she frees him and he lures Tezzeret to Kamigawa and tears off his etherium arm.

When Liliana knocks at his secret door, Gideon interrupts their dinner at Milena's, bloodied, to tell him Sea Gate has fallen, and Jace, admitting to himself that he inadvertently released the Eldrazi, agrees to go while Liliana storms out, leaving Gideon and Jace to step into the carnage of Vorik's camp.

bfz.text: Jace Beleren's part in Zendikar's ruin begins when Nicol Bolas arranges for Sarkhan Vol, Jace and Chandra to converge on the Eye of Ugin and unknowingly reactivate it.

Gideon recruits Jace, and together they find Sea Gate overrun and hold off the Eldrazi so survivors can flee, after which Jace reads Jori En's mind, realizes Ulamog is drawn to concentrations of people, and escapes the Eternal Pilgrims with an illusion that makes them believe they are on fire.

At the Eye the dragon Ugin tells Jace he was one of three planeswalkers manipulated into opening it, but although Jace privately realizes the hedrons might pull the Eldrazi into the physical realm so they could be killed, he keeps the idea to himself and leaves despite Ugin's warnings.

Back at Sea Gate, Gideon lures Ulamog into a ring of hedrons while Jace and Nissa activate the network and trap the titan, before Ob Nixilis takes Gideon, Jace and Nissa prisoner until Chandra frees them and the four swear to stand together as the Gatewatch.

ogw.text: Jace Beleren and Nissa imprison Ulamog in a hedron network at Sea Gate on Ugin's advice, but Ob Nixilis's interference makes the trap fail and he calls Kozilek to join Ulamog.
Chandra frees Jace and his friends from Ob Nixilis, and on the cliffs of Tazeem the four pledge their oaths, founding the Gatewatch.

Jace discovers the leyline pattern needed to anchor the titans, and he and Nissa devise a plan to destroy them permanently, breaking his promise to Ugin, though Jace first has to ask himself what Gideon would say to inspire an army.
With Chandra's massive fire spell the Gatewatch kills the titans in Zendikar's Last Stand, Ugin berates Jace for it, and seriously wounded, Jace flees to Ixalan.

soi.text: Jace Beleren rides toward Stensia with a silent guide who turns into a werewolf, then reveals to a surprised Liliana that he is looking for Sorin Markov, and she sets her zombie servants on him to make a point.

At Markov Manor he finds petrified vampires embedded in the stone and a journal clutched by a dead man, and from it he learns that Sorin made Avacyn to protect humans and concludes that the angels have gone mad and turned on them.

Following the cryptoliths to the Drownyard, Jace is trapped in a dome inside a fisherwoman's mind, sees that every stone points to the circle where angels descend, and accuses Liliana of redirecting the stones, until her Chain Veil backlash and her denial leave him slumped in relief and bound for Thraben, expecting to die.

In Thraben the mad Jace is calmed by Tamiyo, who agrees to anchor his mind, and when Avacyn arrives he freezes her with a mental assault before she breaks free and tortures him, leaving Tamiyo to tell the dying Jace that sometimes stories have to end, and then Avacyn is gone and the plane has lost its protector.

emn.text: At Thraben Cathedral Avacyn overpowers Jace Beleren and Tamiyo until Sorin arrives and destroys the angel he made.

Shielding his mind with Tamiyo's teaching, Jace sees Emrakul for the first time and resolves to bring the Gatewatch to Innistrad, and Tamiyo refuses to come but protects his mind so he can planeswalk away to Chandra's smiling greeting.

On a hill above burning Thraben he overloads the minds of mad werewolves until Gideon slays the mutated survivor, and then he lays out a plan in which Nissa taps the leylines, Gideon clears a path and Chandra channels the energy, refusing Liliana's demand to planeswalk away because they are so close.

When Emrakul unfolds, Jace realizes he has reflexively cast a spell that turns him into a tower shielding everyone from her, and after Tamiyo says Emrakul cannot be destroyed but only bound, a silver beam from the moon draws Emrakul in, though Tamiyo tearfully reveals that Emrakul had taken her over to read the scroll.

akh.text: Jace Beleren and the Gatewatch plan on a Kaladesh rooftop to go to Amonkhet with Liliana navigating, in order to learn what they can of Bolas's plans, and they appear in a sandstorm where undead grab Jace and Jace's illusion lures a wurm away from Liliana.

Inside the city Jace reads an aven vizier's mind and bluffs a cover story, and later, at a mural of Razaketh, he angrily accuses Liliana of breaking the Gatewatch's trust by hiding her demons before taking control of Temmet's mind, and through him the mummies, so they can flee.

Jace later breaks Razaketh's control over Liliana's mind, but he is horrified when she laughs and relishes the killing, and he tells her that he will not stand by if she loses control like that again.

When the Gatewatch attacks Bolas with everything they have, Jace is lured into the dragon's mind, caught in a trap that squeezes it, and facing mind-death he blindly planeswalks away across the Blind Eternities.

hou.text: Jace Beleren warns that Bolas remade the plane in his image and holds the advantage there, and he wonders what Bolas's plan is for the Eternals.
Bolas tells Jace he had hoped for more but expected as much, and then he shatters Jace's mind so that Jace vanishes into the Blind Eternities.

xln.text: Jace Beleren wakes in a bamboo grove with no memory of his own name and finds that a massive force yanks him back when he tries to planeswalk away, but he realizes his visions are illusions he casts himself and takes control of his magic, resolving to become whoever he wants to be.

Descending into his own mind, he finds his spark, and when the Belligerent finds him, its gorgon captain Vraska sees how ill he is, spares him, and invites him to stay with her crew, which he accepts.

Aboard ship Jace learns he can read minds and conjures an illusion of Ravnica for a homesick Vraska, each realizes neither wants to hurt the other, and after the ship is wrecked she reveals to him that they are both planeswalkers, then sees his memory of becoming the Living Guildpact.
Jace then stops Vraska from killing Azor and, as the Living Guildpact, sentences him to solitude on Useless Island.

rix.text: Jace Beleren lies bleeding on a riverbank with his mind broadcasting memories, and Vraska sees him strike the sphinx Alhammarret's mind to ruin, only for his own memories to be ripped away in the backlash as he instinctively planeswalks.

Vraska holds the weeping Jace and apologizes for trying to kill him on Ravnica, and he forgives her, then he recalls Ugin's farewell and realizes it hid a spell that compelled him to planeswalk to Ixalan.

In the throne room Jace declares himself the Living Guildpact and Azor recoils, then admits that the Immortal Sun imprisons planeswalkers and was meant to imprison Nicol Bolas, so Jace sentences him to be caretaker of Useless Island.

Jace shows Vraska his memory of breaking into Bolas's mind, where Ravnica was Bolas's goal, and at her request he seals her memories of him in a warded box so Bolas cannot see them, before resolving that Ravnica must come first and planeswalking to Dominaria.

war.text: During the War of the Spark Bolas orders Tezzeret to activate the Planar Bridge atop the Chamber of the Guildpact, which wrecks the embassy and strips Jace Beleren of his Living Guildpact power.

Jace joins the fight with Lavinia and others, mind-calls everyone to retreat to the Azorius Senate, and lays out the five problems they face, identifying Liliana Vess as the one controlling the Eternals for Bolas.

Jace, Jaya, Teferi and Vivien nearly assassinate Liliana until Bolas destroys the buildings and saves her, and Jace witnesses Gideon sacrificing his life to save Liliana, while he and Vraska agree to try a relationship after Bolas is dead or they are.
After Bolas's faked death, Ugin has Jace create an illusion of the dragon's death and takes Bolas away, Jace hides the truth, and Niv-Mizzet tells him the Firemind is the new Living Guildpact.

m21.text: Jace Beleren is addressed by Liliana, who tells him he always was good at disappearing acts.
On the set's cards he is a planeswalker mage who comments on Chandra's pyrelings.

jmp.text: Jace Beleren hears from Ugin that the hedrons can imprison the Eldrazi, and he doubts it, asking "And how did that work out last time?"
On the set's cards he also names the Eternals.

znr.text: Jace Beleren keeps the secret that Bolas lives and wants to study the lithoform core rather than hear Nissa's plea to help convince Nahiri to destroy it, so Nissa planeswalks back to Zendikar and Jace plans to follow.

He reaches Sea Gate and learns of Murasa from Kesenya's note, is attacked on Murasa by a mushroom-backed monster until Nissa's harabaz elemental destroys it, and agrees to join her in climbing the Skyclave to stop Nahiri.

On the climb Jace tries a mind attack on Nahiri and reads that she is going to the Singing City, where he meets her and is nearly driven mad by the city's song until he casts a silencing spell that also saves her.

Nissa feels betrayed when Jace sides partly with Nahiri, and Jace later seizes the Core with illusions and takes control of Nahiri's mind, but Ashaya returns it to Nissa, who heals Zendikar, and Jace stays to witness its recovery.

cmr.text: Jace Beleren warns that Bolas remade this place in his image, giving him the advantage there, so they must approach carefully.
On the set's cards he is a planeswalker who plunged into his past.

j22.text: Jace Beleren hears from Ugin that the hedrons can imprison the Eldrazi, and he is skeptical, asking "And how did that work out last time?"
On the set's cards he also comments on Chandra.

one.text: Jace Beleren insists the plan stays the same, to get the sylex to the base of the World Tree before it connects through the Blind Eternities, and he admits he is not sure the plane will survive, since the plan is to set off a bomb in its center.

After collapsing from his dose of Halo, Jace wakes and tries to run off because Vraska is calling to him, and the group follows him because he carries the sylex until they find Vraska gravely wounded, who tells him she is already infected and begs him to flee.

Jace casts an illusion of a sunny Ravnican avenue so they can spend one more day together, but Vraska reveals he is infected too, kisses him as the illusion ends, and then, loyal to Phyrexia, stabs his hand with her tail, dosing him with oil, and Jace flees.

Doomed, Jace volunteers to take the sylex, hides the real one behind an illusion that dissolves in Kaya's hands, and pours his grief into it and activates it before Elspeth runs him through and takes the sylex, after which Elesh Norn animates his compleated body.

otj.text: At the Invasion Tree Jace Beleren activates the sylex and surrenders, is compleated, and wakes with a sword through his chest, playing dead behind an illusion until he learns that Elesh Norn has commanded him to go home to Vryn, and he fights the oil in his veins as a virus.

Waking feverish in a ravine, Jace rips out a cable and decides to save Vraska, so he planeswalks to war-torn Ravnica, finds her compleated on a rooftop, performs five simultaneous telepathic feats to reverse her phyresis, and collapses with her in his mother Ranna's home.

Ranna tends them, learns Jace killed Alhammarret, and heals Vraska with a phoenix feather, and Jace and Vraska decide the Multiverse is too broken to fix and settle on a plan of rebirth, though Vraska finds her spark is gone.

Disguised as Ashiok, Jace recruits a raiding team, and when Oko opens the vault Jace takes the sleeping child, whose mind he finds holds a map of the entire Multiverse, and he and Vraska promise to protect Loot as their ward.

tdm.text: Jace Beleren appears to Narset on Tarkir, reveals that he escaped compleation by force of will, and introduces Loot, a creature whose mind holds a map of every Omenpath.

In a flashback Vraska urges him to stop using Loot's mind, but Jace refuses, insisting he must fix everything, and in the present he admits they are trapped in the Meditation Realm where Ugin and a chained dragon, Bolas, wait.
Jace seizes the gem between Ugin's horns, reveals that he wants to reverse Phyrexia's damage and control the realm to save Vraska, and fights Elspeth while Narset rescues the terrified Loot.
When a changed and grief-worn Vraska appears and tells him to stop, Jace shows glimpses of lost futures, but the strain breaks him, the realm begins to unmake itself, and he shatters like glass.

sos.text: Jace Beleren tries to reimagine the Multiverse so that the New Phyrexian Invasion, the Desparkening and the Omenpaths never happened, and after he and Vraska plot a rebirth he steals Ugin's Spirit-Gem in the Meditation Realm, only for the spell to fail because he is only human and shatter him like glass.

A silhouette of a mage in a blue cloak then begins constructing a new reality, and Jace rebuilds himself, discards the parts of himself that dissent to become the Theorist, and creates Tamira as his protege.
Chandra tells Ajani that Jace is alive and still inside her head, and while Ajani insists he is dead and unmade, she says Jace is manipulating archaics and decides he is no longer her friend.
Chandra and Ajani recruit Garruk to stop Jace's plot, and when Vraska stabs the Theorist through the heart the aspects reunite in Jace, who dies in Vraska's arms as his spark flies to Tam.

fra.text: Jace Beleren, traumatized by the New Phyrexian Invasion, sets out to rewrite reality, and when his original plan fails he is unmade in the Meditation Realm, but pieces linger and rebuild him with the need to build a better Multiverse.

Every part of his mind that objected is cut away, leaving the Theorist, who frees Loot, creates the Echoverse intended to be free of suffering, stabilizes it with the dystopian school Hexhaven, and names the newly awakened being Tamira.

The Gatewatch assembles to fight one of its founding members to keep the Multiverse from being overwritten, believing that what was left of Jace could still be reasoned with, and Vraska realizes that Jace knows he is going to die.

As the aberrations reintegrate Jace opens his eyes whole again, gives his friends final messages, and dies in Vraska's arms, unafraid, entrusting his spark to Tam, and Vraska holds his body and weeps.
